messages:
Sasha (oncall): paging — sudden p95 latency cliff on continuous-batching in prod, multiple regions. alerts spiked ~08:12 UTC, errors +5% on streaming API. tagging page.
Michael (eng-oncall): on it. grabbing recent traces and controller logs. @deploy-bot can you post recent rollout history for cb-controller?
deploy-bot: recent deployments for namespace=prod: continuous-batch-controller v2.13.4 -> v2.13.6 (03:40 UTC), autoscaler config change (04:50 UTC), prefetch-heuristic toggle enabled (07:58 UTC).
Nora (infra): KV cache eviction rate jumped 7.8x across us-west-2 nodes starting 08:11. Prefetch queue depth also skyrocketed. Suspect prefetch heuristic interacting poorly under high concurrency.
Lee (runtime): Confirmed. Microbatch window widened at high concurrency; we see microbatch_size reaching 48-64 on some hosts (expected target 16-32). That increases in-flight KV entries and causes eviction spiral + DB pressure.
Olivia (sre): Customers that hit p95 errors are those with sustained 300-800 rps bursts, mostly chat streaming. Most impact is increased latency and occasional 503s when we hit KV cache misses + eviction IO.
Sasha (oncall): Recommended short-term mitigations? we need something safe and fast.
Michael (eng-oncall): Propose 3-step live mitigation: 1) disable prefetch heuristic globally (cheap config flip) 2) reduce max_microbatch_size from 64->8 (controller config) 3) enable temporary token-throttling for noisy clients. Rollout via canary 10% -> 50% -> 100%.
Nora (infra): Disabling prefetch should immediately reduce prefetch queue depth and KV churn. Microbatch cap change needs controller rollout.
Lee (runtime): Agree. Also add a temporary guard in batching: if queueing latency > 50ms, hard cap microbatch to 8. We can implement config flip via configmap to avoid full binary rollout.
Michael (eng-oncall): I'll start the canary. Command: ```kubectl -n prod set env configmap/continuous-batch-config PREFETCH_ENABLED=false && kubectl -n prod apply -f cb-configmap.yaml``` Rolling restart for canary subset: ```kubectl rollout restart deployment/continuous-batch-controller --selector=canary=true```
deploy-bot: canary rollout started (10% of replicas). rollout_id=rb-176987. watching pods.
incident-bot: alert suppression enabled for "continuous-batch latency" for 30m while mitigation in progress.
Sasha (oncall): Support: inform top-tier customers that we're actively mitigating; add note an incident may affect streaming latency. @olivia please coordinate comms.
Olivia (sre): messaging draft: "We're investigating increased streaming latency; mitigation underway. No data loss expected. We'll update at 30min intervals." Posting to status slack channel and start standby for support.
Michael (eng-oncall): Canary metrics at +2m: p95 latency for canary hosts dropped ~65ms, KV eviction-rate down 58%, prefetch queue depth reduced to baseline.
Nora (infra): DB IO also trending down. Good sign.
Lee (runtime): Starting 50% rollout: ```kubectl label deployment continuous-batch-controller canary=true --overwrite --selector=rollout-phase=mid && kubectl rollout restart -n prod deployment/continuous-batch-controller --selector=rollout-phase=mid``` (ops done)
deploy-bot: 50% rollout in progress.
Michael (eng-oncall): Also applied controller config to set MAX_MICROBATCH_SIZE=8 via configmap patch: ```kubectl patch configmap cb-config -n prod --patch 'data:{"MAX_MICROBATCH_SIZE":"8"}'``` Restart triggered in canary group.
Sasha (oncall): Any customer regressions from smaller microbatches (e.g., throughput drops)?
Olivia (sre): Early telemetry shows slight throughput reduction for very high-batched workloads but overall latency improved; we've not seen new 5xx spikes. Inform customers with large sustained throughput that we may throttle briefly.
Lee (runtime): After 80% rollout, microbatch distribution centered at 6-8, KV-hit-rate improved 32% and tail latencies normalized.
Michael (eng-oncall): Moving to full 100% rollout now.
deploy-bot: Full rollout complete. rollout_id=rb-176987, status=success.
incident-bot: automated post-mitigation checks: latency p95 within SLA thresholds, error-rate within baseline. Generating incident report draft.
Sasha (oncall): Great. Next steps: 1) keep prefetch disabled until we ship heuristic fix 2) create follow-up task to add queueing-based hard cap in batching code 3) triage root cause of prefetch heuristic regression and add canary tests.
Nora (infra): I'll open infra ticket: "prefetch-heuristic-thrash -> investigate eviction feedback loop" and attach eviction/log dumps.
Lee (runtime): I'll PR a batching-guard that clamps microbatch when queueing latency > threshold and add unit/integration tests.
Olivia (sre): I'll coordinate postmortem and customer impact summary. Early estimate: 5 customers saw transient latency increases, 3 of which had retries or short reconnects; no data loss. Will include precise numbers after metric queries.
Michael (eng-oncall): Closing pager and handing off to runbook owners for postmortem. Thanks team :thumbsup:
Sasha (oncall): Closing thread once postmortem link posted. Good job everyone.
